Zelensky pushes for trilateral talks "no later than early November" — sooner than Moscow's "after Nov. 10"

After the St. Petersburg readout landed in the evening brief (Putin agreed "in principle" to trilateral talks after Nov. 10, at technical level), Zelensky told journalists on his way back to Kyiv that Ukraine supports a US proposal for three-way talks at negotiator level "as soon as possible, preferably no later than early November." He said Kyiv has feedback that Russia supports a trilateral meeting at negotiating-team level, and that the US "will do everything to ensure that the meeting takes place as early as possible, in November." He also said Kyiv supports "any proposals for a ceasefire, an end to the war, an energy ceasefire as well as humanitarian initiatives." So the two sides are now publicly aligned on the format — but not yet on the date, and not on whether Putin himself ever sits at the table. Reuters

US orders diplomats and families out of Saudi Arabia as Houthi strikes hit an airport and an oilfield in one day

The State Department ordered the departure of non-emergency US government employees and their family members from Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, and US officials told Reuters it plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions across the Gulf. Spokesman Tommy Pigott cited Houthi attacks "on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions." The order came after two deadly attacks Wednesday: one person killed and eight injured at Dammam's King Fahd International Airport, and two killed at Aramco's Shaybah oilfield (see below). The US Embassy in Riyadh also issued a security alert warning of possible further Houthi attacks. This is the sharpest US step yet in the Saudi-Houthi escalation — a formal ordered departure, not just a travel warning. Reuters via Devdiscourse · Reuters (Dammam)

Putin agrees "in principle" to trilateral talks after Nov. 10 — but not at the leaders' table

Putin agrees "in principle" to trilateral talks after Nov. 10 — but not at the leaders' table

The readout from the Witkoff–Putin meeting finally landed this afternoon: Kremlin foreign-policy adviser Yuri Ushakov said Putin agreed "in principle" that trilateral US–Russia–Ukraine talks will continue after Nov. 10, focused on "building a security system for Russia and Ukraine after the conflict ends." A US official added the talks would happen "at the technical level" — meaning Putin himself won't sit down with Trump or Zelensky. Both sides accepted the trilateral format (Ukraine in Oslo Tuesday, Russia in St. Petersburg today), and the US readout cited "progress" on a post-war economic plan and European security architecture. The catch, per CNN: no indication Russia has budged on its maximalist positions — full Donbas, a shrunken Ukrainian military, no NATO. Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev separately said the US–Russia diesel deal goes ahead despite European criticism. CNN · NY Post

He drew a line at giving up the Donbas — "not fair" — and at any deal negotiated without Ukraine ("don't speak about us without us"). PHP2Shell: emergency patches out today for two critical PHP flaws — NSA, FBI and CISA say patch now or take systems offline

PHP released fixes Wednesday (8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35) for CVE-2026-109618 (RCE via out-of-memory corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (RCE via stale global state), both CVSS 9.2, both allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. Cloudflare says it is already seeing early attack attempts and has deployed WAF rules; watchTowr honeypots logged exploitation attempts; several European government sites went offline to patch. CISA had not observed exploitation as of publication, and neither CVE is on KEV yet — but exploit code is circulating publicly, so this is a patch-now, not patch-soon, item. LiteLLM 1.107.0 was hijacked on PyPI for ~1¾ hours — a credential stealer in one of AI's most-used plumbing packages

BerriAI confirmed its LiteLLM 1.107.0 release, published to PyPI and Docker on Wednesday, "contained compiled malware which steals credentials and loads remote-code execution tools." Attackers used three engineers' GitHub accounts via apparently stolen GitHub CLI tokens, overrode branch protection, and built the release from a lookalike "Berri-AI" copy of the repo. Seven malicious wheels were live on PyPI 11:39–13:23 UTC; tainted Docker images (including latest) stayed up until 14:20 UTC. The payload steals SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI/CD secrets, browser passwords and LLM provider keys, and runs on any Python startup — even without importing litellm. Wiz already observed stolen AWS credentials being validated from 16:20 UTC, consistent with LLMjacking. If you installed or ran 1.107.0, rotate everything it could have touched; 1.106.2 and the release candidates are clean. This is LiteLLM's second hijack this year. GCC foreign ministers met in Manama Sunday, condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, and invoked the GCC joint defence pact

  • GCC foreign ministers met in Manama Sunday, condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, and invoked the GCC joint defence pact — an attack on one member "affects all six." They called for tighter UN arms-embargo enforcement and formal terrorist designation for the Houthis. Saudi FM also met Lavrov separately to discuss Yemen and Hormuz navigation.
